summary: An excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's novel Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (labeled "Book 11 — part 39") in which Rebecca is scolded by her Aunt Miranda for leaving the house unsecured and careless while she went to a school exhibition wearing her pink dress and carrying a parasol. Miranda lists Rebecca's transgressions: she dropped a handkerchief, left a window screen out, left lunch uncleared, and left the side door unlocked. Rebecca tearfully explains she was late, rushed back to school, and feared a black mark. Miranda closes by reproaching her for not trying to make less trouble in a house that is not her own.
one_line: Aunt Miranda scolds Rebecca for leaving the house unlocked and careless after she secretly wore her pink dress and parasol to a school exhibition.
key_facts: Rebecca did not ask Aunt Miranda's permission before wearing the pink dress and parasol to school.
Rebecca said she had intended to ask at noontime but could not because Miranda was not at home.
Rebecca admitted she was not certain Miranda would refuse, but thought it was worth the risk because the event was almost a real exhibition at school.
Miranda called the parasol business "exhibition enough by yourself" and asked whether Rebecca was exhibiting her parasol.
Rebecca and Emma Jane spoke a dialogue about a city girl and a country girl at the school exhibition.
Rebecca said the parasol was silly but was the only time in her whole life she had anything to match it.
Miranda said Rebecca dropped her handkerchief on the way up the front stairs, so she did not hide her tracks.
Miranda said Rebecca left the screen out of her bedroom window, letting flies come into the house.
Miranda said Rebecca never cleared away her lunch or put away a dish.
Miranda said Rebecca left the side door unlocked from half past twelve to three o'clock.
Rebecca said she was trimming the schoolroom, got belated, and ran all the way home.
Rebecca feared being late and receiving her first black mark on a Friday afternoon with the minister's wife, the doctor's wife and the school committee present.
Miranda quoted the proverb: "An ounce of good behavior is worth a pound of repentance."
